1.w: Then Zophar the Naamathite spoke up and said:

2.w: “Should not this abundance of words be answered, or should this talkative man be vindicated?

3.w: Should people remain silent at your idle talk, and should no one rebuke you when you mock?

4.w: For you have said, ‘My teaching is flawless, and I am pure in your sight.’

5.w: But if only God would speak, if only he would open his lips against you

6.w: and reveal to you the secrets of wisdom— for true wisdom has two sides — so that you would know that God has forgiven some of your sins.

7.w: “Can you discover the essence of God? Can you find out the perfection of the Almighty?

8.w: It is higher than the heavens—what can you do? It is deeper than Sheol —what can you know?

9.w: Its measure is longer than the earth and broader than the sea.

10.w: If he comes by and confines you and convenes a court, then who can prevent him?

11.w: For he knows deceitful men; when he sees evil, will he not consider it?

12.w: But an empty man will become wise, when a wild donkey’s colt is born a human being.

13.w: “As for you, if you prove faithful, and if you stretch out your hands toward him,

14.w: if iniquity is in your hand—put it far away, and do not let evil reside in your tents.

15.w: For then you will lift up your face without blemish; you will be securely established and will not fear.

16.w: For you will forget your trouble; you will remember it like water that has flowed away.

17.w: And life will be brighter than the noonday; though there be darkness, it will be like the morning.

18.w: And you will be secure because there is hope; you will be protected and will take your rest in safety.

19.w: You will lie down with no one to make you afraid, and many will seek your favor.

20.w: But the eyes of the wicked fail, and escape eludes them; their one hope is to breathe their last.”
